headline: Middleby beats guidance despite divestiture loss
summary_short: Middleby's Q1 2026 net sales rose 15.0% y/y to $840M (11.9% organic); continuing-operations diluted EPS of $1.81 (Adjusted $2.16) beat the high end of guidance, but a $135.4M discontinued-operations loss tied to the pending Food Processing spin-off swung reported net income to a $50.1M loss (-$1.06 diluted EPS).
summary_long: Net sales rose 15.0% y/y to $839.9M (11.9% organic; Commercial Foodservice +8.1% organic, Food Processing +25.0% organic). Operating income of $133.4M included $9.9M of strategic transaction costs tied to the pending three-way portfolio split; Adjusted EBITDA rose to $180.6M from $161.5M. Continuing-operations diluted EPS of $1.81 (Adjusted $2.16) topped the high end of prior guidance. Reported net income swung to a $50.1M loss (-$1.06 diluted EPS) solely on a $135.4M after-tax loss from discontinued operations tied to the Food Processing spin-off, on track for July 6, 2026. Middleby raised FY2026 guidance to $3.36-3.44B revenue and $9.54-9.70 Adjusted EPS. Cash fell to $177.1M and long-term debt to $1,829.9M after $520M+ of YTD buybacks; net leverage stood at 2.3x.

drivers.explanation: Organic net sales grew 11.9% (Commercial Foodservice +8.1%, Food Processing +25.0%), plus acquisitions (+1.0%) and favorable foreign exchange (+2.0%).
Gross profit rose 10.5% on higher volume, but gross margin fell to 38.5% from 40.1% as cost of sales grew faster (+18.0%) than net sales (+15.0%).
Topline growth and volume leverage were partly offset by $9.9M of strategic transaction costs tied to the pending three-way portfolio separation.

Swung to a net loss entirely due to a $135.4M after-tax loss from discontinued operations tied to the Food Processing spin-off; continuing-operations net earnings were flat at $85.3M vs $85.1M a year ago.
Follows directly from the discontinued-operations loss; continuing-operations diluted EPS was $1.81 and Adjusted EPS $2.16, both above the high end of prior guidance.
Tracks revenue growth and operating leverage; the company's own non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA rose to $180.6M from $161.5M, with Commercial Foodservice margin at 25.7% and Food Processing at 18.5%.

Cash fell on $684.7M of net financing outflows, including over $520M of YTD share buybacks, partly offset by $556.5M of investing inflows including $564.6M from selling a 51% stake in Residential Kitchen Equipment Group.
Debt declined as proceeds from the Residential Kitchen Equipment Group stake sale and quarterly cash flow were applied against borrowings, ending the quarter at 2.3x net leverage.
Results exceeded the high end of Q1 guidance for revenue, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EPS; the company raised FY2026 guidance and remains on track to spin off Food Processing on July 6, 2026.
